title: Jhonny Bobier breaks silence on ‘Tatsulok’ controversy, says he was ‘intentionally humiliated’
summary: Filmmaker Jhonny Bobier has finally spoken up about the controversy surrounding his film “Tatsulok,” saying he felt he was deliberately put in an embarrassing situation over allegations that he…

blocks.text: Filmmaker Jhonny Bobier has finally spoken up about the controversy surrounding his film “Tatsulok,” saying he felt he was deliberately put in an embarrassing situation over allegations that he screened it publicly using fake MTRCB permit. In a video statement sent to GMA News Online, Bobier denied having anything to do with the alleged falsified Permit to Exhibit (PTE) linked to “Tatsulok Trilogy” and Tanajuan Pelikula Production. “I had nothing to do with that alleged fake MTRCB permit. I do not know where it came from,” Bobier said, as quoted by GMA News Online. The Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) earlier said “Tatsulok” had not undergone its review and classification process and had no valid PTE. The agency also said it discovered a fake permit connected to the film and its production company. Bobier, however, maintained that he never obtained an MTRCB permit for the film’s August 21 premiere. According to his account, this was his first time independently handling the requirements for a public film screening, after previously having such matters handled through film festivals. He said he relied on a Gateway Cineplex representative who handled the agreement for the screening and believed the cinema would inform him about the necessary requirements. Bobier also claimed he understood that a permit was needed for the planned August 29 public screening, not the August 21 premiere. The situation came to a head during the premiere when a cinema representative allegedly asked him for an MTRCB permit and warned that the screening could be stopped without one. Bobier said he decided to proceed with the event because the venue had already been paid for and guests were already waiting to watch the film. It was the timing of the issue that particularly troubled him. The director described the cinema management's decision to raise the permit concern at the last minute as suspicious, arguing that he should have been informed earlier if the document was a requirement. More importantly, Bobier said the incident left him feeling deliberately embarrassed in front of the people who had supported his film. “I cannot help but feel that they tried to humiliate me and embarrass me in front of those people who supported my film,” Bobier said. He further described the experience as being “intentionally cornered and humiliated,” saying it made him appear irresponsible for an administrative issue he claimed he did not create or know about. The filmmaker's comments come after Gateway Cineplex 18 issued a public notice on August 26 saying it was not associated with Tanajuan Pelikula or the planned August 29 screening of “Tatsulok.” The cinema also said the film would not be shown at any of its cinemas. Bobier said the notice prompted him to finally give his own account of what happened. He is now working with his lawyer and is seeking due process as the controversy continues.
